tagline: Down an old Red River channel from Natchitoches to Cloutierville.
intro: From Natchitoches, founded in 1714 and the oldest permanent settlement in the Louisiana Purchase, the byway follows Cane River south. It was once a main channel of the Red River, until the Red moved east in 1836, and it is an oxbow lake now. Corn and soybean farms, sugar cane and pecan orchards come down toward the red-soil banks.

Along this river grew a Creole culture of free people of color, centered on Melrose and the St. Augustine church at Isle Brevelle, the first Catholic church in the country built and supported by free people of color. The road ends at Cloutierville, where Kate Chopin once owned the old plantation house.

moments.title: Natchitoches
moments.text: Front Street is still paved in brick, and when it was repaired the workers took up each brick, numbered it, cleaned it and laid it back where it came from.

moments.title: Oakland Plantation
moments.text: On a bend of Cane River Lake, the Prud'homme cotton plantation, worked by enslaved people, survives as an unusually intact French Creole plantation complex, now part of the national park.

moments.title: Melrose Plantation
moments.text: Louis Metoyer, son of the freed slave Marie Thérèse Coincoin, began the big house about 1832, and later Clementine Hunter lived here and sold her first paintings for as little as 25 cents.
